verdicts.attacks: Attack 1 (effort honesty): '2 focused days certain' is honest for Phases 1-2, but the framing buries that the probable branch is the actual fix — at 33% capture, Phase 3 firing is likely, so the real pre-stranger budget is 2 OR 6-7 days and should be planned as a fork, not a footnote. The measure-first core survived my strongest attack (skip straight to SpeechAnalyzer): today's 8 unmeasured commits plausibly moved the number (the 250-word collapse class was the single largest recorded loss, and taskHint=.dictation is a known large lever), so engine-first genuinely risks misattribution — the spec's pre-registered §8 gate is the right discipline, not process theater. Attack 2 (pre/post call, partially landed): Phase 3's PRE status silently assumes the STRANGER'S phone runs iOS 26 — an arm behind @available(iOS 26,*) does nothing for a stranger on iOS 18, whose week runs on SFSpeech regardless; the pre/post analysis never screens the stranger's hardware. Attack 3 (duplicated work): Phase 2's live session duplicates cluster C's field protocol (same cable build, same second human, same journal export, same scorer shape); as written, A would burn the session without C's speaker-score instrument, wasting it for C. Attack 4 (what the stranger notices): the correctly-deferred VAD/seq/boot_id refusal is the best over-engineering call in the whole set — timestamps with no consumer, honestly named.
verdicts.required_changes: (1) Merge Phase 2 with C's protocol into ONE recorded session, with C's journal instrument landed first so the session yields both capture and speaker numbers. (2) Add to the §8 branch condition: 'and the recruited stranger's device runs iOS 26' — otherwise the engine fork is moot for leg 6 and the week's honest posture is measured-SFSpeech. (3) Budget Phase 3 in the calendar as probable, not exceptional, and build the arm behind the engine seam cluster G specifies so PhoneListener is extracted once.

verdicts.cluster: B — Segment-granularity triage, ask valve, meeting window
verdicts.attacks: Attack 1 (pre/post): I tried to kill PRE by arguing the shard tape converts the danger into mere deafness — thin lines go inert, not wrong — so the week survives on per-line judging. It half-worked: the wrong-act risk is one-guard-away rather than active. But it fails as a kill because leg 6 demands a CLEAN week, and a week of silently-missed conversations fails 'she caught what mattered' just as surely; plus the tape's declared expiry IS this build (Law 2), and shipping the stranger week on standing tape whose expiry was reachable is the loop the laws exist to break. PRE stands. Attack 2 (the design's own contradiction): extracting anticipy_core.py:1568-1961 into _ambient_verdict relocates ~400 scar-laden lines — the exact 'relocation is how lessons get re-learned' argument cluster E used to reject ITS candidate A. The design has no behavior-pin before the extraction. Attack 3 (shadow validity): 2-3 days of one owner's ambient traffic can produce near-zero diffs on quiet days, making 'clean diffs' vacuously true — the flip criterion as written can be satisfied by silence. Attack 4 (effort): 7-9 days is the optimistic edge for pure pieces + prompt + triggers + funnel extraction + stamps + sweep + adversarial rounds; honest as a range, but expect the top of it. Latency attack (3s to 45s) failed: a stranger has no baseline and the fast lane covers direct address.
verdicts.required_changes: (1) Land the _ambient_verdict extraction as its own commit with replay_call.py proving verdict-identical behavior pre/post extraction BEFORE any segment path exists. (2) Pre-register what a shadow day must contain: at least one scripted rig conversation per soak day so 'clean diffs' can never be vacuous. (3) Sequence after H Stage 1 and E so worker.py churns once, and rebase the extraction on their landed diffs. (4) Pre-register the flip criteria (diff count, categories tolerated) before the soak starts, same discipline as A/C/H.

verdicts.attacks: Attack 1 (push it post-stranger): argued the honesty wall + confirmation gate already bound the damage, so measurement can wait. Failed — the tagger-on vs tagger-dark decision for the stranger build cannot be made blind (a false-owner puts promises in a stranger's mouth; both options are safe but only one is honest to pick unmeasured), and the unguarded in_meeting go-ahead is a genuine week-ender: someone else's 'okay let's do it' releasing a held consequential card during the exact posture built because in_conversation missed the Tejas call. Attack 2 (its refusal of the Brief): 'unattributed lines never mint' correctly refused — with 97% no-verdict measured, that bar is deafness, and the confirmation tap already is the attribution of last resort; this is the best Law-5 reasoning in the set. Attack 3 (over-engineering): five conditions x 10 turns is borderline gold-plating for a floor measurement — but it costs one hour of recording, and the Meet-at-speaker-volume condition is the recorded failure condition, so it stands. Attack 4 (effort): ~3 days honest; calendar risk is only the second human, which merging with A's session halves. The scale-trap honesty (floors, not certification) is stated, not hidden.
verdicts.required_changes: (1) Merge the field session with A Phase 2 — one build, one second human, two scorers; instrument lands first or the session is wasted for the speaker half. (2) Land the in_meeting go-ahead guard + test in the measurement-build window, not after — it is 0.25d and week-critical independent of the measurement outcome. (3) Reconcile with A Task 4: build the onboarding enrollment page now, gate its EXPOSURE on the voice leg's verdict (hidden when the tagger ships dark — the available=false path is already proven safe).

verdicts.attacks: Attack 1 (the strongest pre/post attack in the set): a COLD stranger has a days-old, thin profile — the failure requires learn-contradict-reassert inside seven days, the least probable week-ender in the pre-stranger set, and forget_fact ('forget that') ALREADY exists as a recovery path the design undersells. The attack demotes but does not kill PRE: briefings lead with profile facts every session, day-zero interview facts DO get corrected mid-week, and a re-asserted dead fact is the exact 'what?' moment — but it is a day-3+ risk, not day-one, and it is recoverable in-week via the veto where capture/attribution failures are not. Attack 2 (over-engineering for the stage): the nightly reconcile sweep's main value is healing the OWNER'S legacy DB — irrelevant to a cold stranger whose DB is empty; building it pre-stranger exceeds what the stage needs. Attack 3 (effort): 3 days honest — self-contained in memory.py, FakeLLM and additive-migration precedents exist; the two deterministic guards (temporal, provenance fence) are genuinely structure-not-meaning and the crash-replay/resurrection adversarial cases are already closed in the design. Candidate D (role-slot ontology) correctly refused as rewrite-adjacent.
verdicts.required_changes: (1) Split: write-time supersession pre-stranger (~2d), nightly reconcile post-stranger. (2) Schedule it into B's shadow-soak days (soak is passive observation; memory.py is disjoint from B's diff except a one-line nightly hook) — the metronome-compatible use of dead calendar. (3) Mark it first-to-cut if the calendar squeezes, and teach 'forget that' in stranger onboarding as the hedge either way.

verdicts.attacks: Attack 1 (is the hole real): verified in this checkout — uninvited_sent_today counts only rows whose params contains 'uninvited', and events has no params column, so the advertised 3/day cap counts approximately nothing; the 10+-texts busy-week scenario is legal today. PRE is unambiguous: mid-meeting buzzes on a working stranger and a text flood are one-wrong-interruption week-enders, active from day one. Attack 2 (busy-defer vs the speak-at-once scar): tried to kill deferring stuck-job asks on room_busy using the recorded immediacy decision at :2938-2950 — failed: a 2-minute room-busy defer is not the rejected 9-hour defer, and asking into his meeting IS the recorded 2026-08-23 failure shape. Attack 3 (effort): 2.5-3 days is credible precisely because the hard work (the eleven-incident non-recreation table) is already done in the design; the wiring is 3-line checks at existing decision points. Attack 4 (candidate selection): rejecting the outbox collection (second source of truth = webhook-drift shape), notify_owner governance (post-compose checks = paid-compose scar), and the moments batcher (over-silencing = the product's named worst failure) is the cleanest over-engineering refusal in the set. The one-day TAPE clause carries a leg — Law 2 clean. The _NON_ANSWER flag is correct good citizenship.
verdicts.required_changes: None material to the design. Sequencing only: land before B so worker.py churns once, and B's shadow phase must distinguish budget refusals from verdict diffs (E's refusal reasons will appear in B's shadow logs).

verdicts.attacks: Attack 1 (are the defects real): verified locally — PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy declares exactly UserDefaults + FileTimestamp with no SystemBootTime dict, project.yml has no postBuildScripts, and the controlled b47-b50 on/off correlation plus the nm-proven sysctl imports make both defects independently established; fixing both in one upload weakens attribution but the visibility loop (ASC API polling + readable admin email) converts any residual failure into a named ITMS reason, which is the correct trade. Attack 2 (THE missed dependency — strongest single attack across all eight clusters): processingState VALID is not 'a stranger can install.' A cold stranger is an EXTERNAL TestFlight tester, which requires an external test group and Beta App Review approval of the first build in it — its own multi-day Apple clock and its own rejection surface, and this app's always-on mic + background audio is exactly what Beta review probes. The design's definition of done stops at VALID plus a team-device install; as written, leg 6 could still be blocked AFTER this cluster reports green. Attack 3 (effort): 1.5-2.5 focused days honest, but calendar time is Apple-latency-dominated and unbounded on a re-reject — which is the argument for running it first, not later. Mutation-testing the gates and asserting sherpa symbols PRESENT (so the fix cannot pass by regressing to the empty link) is exemplary Law-6 work.
verdicts.required_changes: (1) Extend done to: external-group invite accepted and installed on a non-team phone, with enrollment loading the speaker engine. (2) On VALID, immediately create the external group and submit for Beta App Review; pre-write review notes justifying background audio and the always-listening mic. (3) Run this cluster FIRST so both Apple clocks tick under all subsequent work.

verdicts.cluster: G — Local-first violated by the pendant lane
verdicts.attacks: Attack 1 (pre/post): the POST call is airtight and verified — firmware/BUILD_RECEIPT.json says BUILT_AND_VERIFIED_NOT_FLASHED, no stranger can hold a pendant, the Deepgram path cannot fire without paired hardware, and 5 days here would delay leg 6 for a lane with zero week exposure; the stranger would never notice any of Stages 1-4. Stage 0 (the tripwire making flash-with-Deepgram-present a red gate) is correctly PRE: half a day, converts FOLLOWUPS prose into an unshippable-by-accident invariant. Attack 2 (effort honesty): 2 days for extracting RecognitionEngine from the most battle-scarred 731 lines in the app is optimistic — expect 3-4, and the two-concurrent-recognition-tasks OS question is a real unknown the design at least commits to benching rather than guessing. Post-stranger placement makes the optimism non-fatal. Attack 3 (candidate discipline): refusing the Local/Cloud toggle (rule 1 violated on demand) and killing the naive LocalTranscriber revival (the documented one-line-per-conversation bug) are both correct; candidate C's sherpa-ASR rejection on TestFlight-payload grounds shows real cross-cluster awareness of F.

verdicts.attacks: Attack 1 (is the bypass real): verified against anticipy-tejas — touches is threaded only at the ambient site (:1619) and the direct-lane hold calls is_consequential(goal, params, explicit=explicit) with no touches, so a typed consequential ask with a verb outside _VERBS mints unheld, discarding a 'world' declaration the model already made. A stranger TYPES things on day one; this is the trust spine and PRE for the fix is right. Attack 2 (pre/post over-scope — landed): Stage 2 (1.5d corpus labeling + three-classifier eval) changes ZERO runtime behavior; it exists solely to authorize Stage 3's deletion, and Stage 3 is post-stranger by the design's own admission (the fallback's in-week failure mode is one extra tap). So Stage 2 belongs post-week or in B's soak idle days — the claimed ~3 pre-stranger days is really 1.5. Attack 3 (Law 2): Stage 0's observation that leg 4 is green TODAY while the tape stands is a real caught gap — the red-leg-from-day-one is the design's best piece. Attack 4 (end-state discipline): deny-list-outranks-declaration, hold-on-undeclared+dead-model, and candidate C acknowledged as the true end state but correctly deferred — no over-engineering; candidate D correctly rejected as the tape-outliving-its-expiry loop shape.
verdicts.required_changes: (1) Re-scope pre-stranger to Stage 0 + Stage 1 only (~1.5d): red leg, thread touches into the direct lane (and :1527/:3129), persist the channel on job rows, partitions read the stored field. (2) The direct-lane behavioral test (typed world-goal lands awaiting_approval) ships in the same commit as the fix. (3) Stage 2 runs post-week or during B's shadow soak; Stage 3 stays post-week gated on the eval's frozen death criterion.

ordering:
LEG-6 CRITICAL PATH (pre-stranger; ~17-19 focused days as re-scoped, +4-5 if the engine fork fires; the eight clusters as submitted claimed ~3.5 days more than the stage needs — H Stage 2 out, D trimmed and soak-overlapped, G all-but-Stage-0 out):

1. F (TestFlight): strip script + SystemBootTime manifest + IPA audit + ASC polling gate, upload build 77, request the ASC admin invite, and ON VALID immediately create the external tester group and submit for Beta App Review with pre-written mic/background-audio notes — it owns the two longest external clocks (Apple processing AND Beta review) and the week cannot start without it; ~1 focused day, with Apple's waits running under everything below. G Stage 0 (the Deepgram/flash tripwire, 0.5d) lands as the same-day filler while Apple processes — free, and it makes the latent law violation unshippable by accident.

2. The measurement build: C's journal instrument (speaker-score ListenEvent + Settings export) FIRST, then A Phase 1 (EnrollmentInvite + onboarding page + tejas_gate leg 9 + the capture-span refinement) plus C's in_meeting go-ahead guard + test — everything the single merged field session needs, and the guard is a 0.25d week-critical fix that should not wait for the measurement's outcome. (~2d)

3. The merged live session: A Phase 2 and C's five-condition protocol as ONE cable-installed recording day (owner + one second human, Meet-at-speaker-volume included), scored by both scorers into research/evals/ — this one day converts 8 repo-green capture commits into measured numbers AND decides the two forks everything downstream depends on: engine yes/no (§8) and tagger on/dark. Earliest possible because it forks the plan. (~1.5d incl. scoring and write-up)

4. H Stages 0+1: red leg while _READ_ONLY_RE exists, thread touches into the direct lane/:1527/:3129, persist the channel, partitions read stored consequence, behavioral test in the same commit — closes the typed-ask confirmation bypass a stranger hits the first time they text her, and its small worker/core diff lands before B churns the same files. (~1.5d; Stages 2-3 post-week)

5. E: the uninvited ledger (events.uninvited flag), shared 3/day budget across FYI/clock/ask/digest, busy-defer on the four unguarded paths, outbound_gate with the live round-trip leg — makes the advertised cap actually count and stops mid-meeting buzzes, the other day-one week-ender; worker.py edits land before B's big diff. (~3d incl. the one-day TAPE-clause wait, which overlaps step 6/7)

6. A Phase 3 ONLY IF the §8 gate fired AND the recruited stranger's phone runs iOS 26: SpeechAnalyzer arm behind the engine seam G specified, both-arms-logged day, re-measure with the same scorer — capture is the floor, and B's shadow must soak on post-fix traffic or its diffs describe a system that no longer exists. If §8 did not fire, skip and spend nothing. (+3-5d conditional)

7. B: segment triage in strict internal order — pure pieces, then the _ambient_verdict extraction as its own commit with a pre/post replay pin proving identical verdicts, then replay evals, then the 2-3 day live shadow soak with one scripted rig conversation per day and pre-registered flip criteria, then the flip commit deleting shard_too_thin and rewriting leg 2, then deploy + fingerprint + live rig proof — the long pole and the tape's declared expiry; last among builds because it needs the quietest tree, the live-verified 4888612d lineage, and representative capture. (~7-9d + soak calendar)

8. D write-time supersession (~2d), executed DURING B's shadow-soak days — the soak is passive observation and memory.py is disjoint from B's diff, so this is the metronome-compatible use of otherwise dead calendar; nightly reconcile deferred post-week. First candidate to cut if the calendar squeezes: forget_fact is the standing in-week recovery path.

9. Pre-week freeze + cold-start rehearsal (~1d): every gate green against LIVE (tejas_gate 9/9, done_gate 1-5, outbound_gate, the voice leg with its verdict applied to tagger exposure, testflight_gate for the shipped build number), then one full dry-run of stranger onboarding on a fresh account — new owner ref, empty memory DB, Twilio provisioning, welcome text, day-zero interview, voice enrollment page — because no cluster owns the cold-start path the stranger hits first.

10. THE STRANGER WEEK: nothing ships during it; the daily question is 'was yesterday clean'; journals and events collected daily so a failed week produces the next paired eval instead of an anecdote.

POST-STRANGER, in order: H Stage 2 (frozen corpus eval — can also fill soak days) then H Stage 3 (delete _READ_ONLY_RE under the death criterion); B's deferred pieces (backfill re-triage, per-segment memory extraction, cheap gate tier); D's nightly reconcile; G Stages 1-4 (libopus decode, RecognitionEngine extraction, Deepgram deletion) when firmware flashing is actually scheduled; A's VAD/Smart Turn/envelope fields (pendant era, no consumers today); C's naming-a-voice UX, battery measurement, and passive coverage monitor. Rationale for the overall shape: front-load the irreversible external clocks (F), buy the two fork-deciding numbers with one merged session (2-3), close the three cheap active week-enders (4-5: typed bypass, text flood, meeting go-ahead), resolve the capture fork (6), then run the one long build with its safety soak (7) using its dead calendar for the one self-contained pre-stranger remainder (8), freeze, rehearse, and only then invite the stranger.
cross_cutting: CONFLICTS AND SHARED DECISIONS: (1) Two checkouts, one truth — the eight recommendations cite files in BOTH /Users/josegaelcruzlopez/Desktop/anticipy-omize (cwd; clusters A, B, F partially) and /Users/josegaelcruzlopez/Desktop/anticipy-tejas (clusters C, D, E, H explicitly). I verified the touches/shard_too_thin claims hold in anticipy-tejas but NOT in anticipy-omize (no touches threading, no shard_too_thin there — it is a divergent lineage). Before day one, declare which checkout is canonical and reconcile the branches, or gates will go green against a tree prod is not serving — the exact Law-3 scar (stale prod, twice) at repo scale. (2) Merged measurement session — A Phase 2 and C's field protocol are the same physical event (one cable build, one second human, one hour of scripted conversation, journal export, scorer); running them separately wastes a day and a scheduling dependency, and running A's first without C's instrument wastes the session for the speaker half. C's instrument lands first; one session, two scorers, two eval directories. (3) Enrollment-in-onboarding — A Task 4 builds the page now; C says onboarding exposure only after the voice leg is green. Reconciliation: build in step 2, expose per C's verdict (page hidden when the tagger ships dark; SpeakerTagger.available=false is the proven-safe path). (4) The engine seam — A Phase 3's SpeechAnalyzer arm and G's RecognitionEngine name the same abstraction; whoever builds first owns the seam and the other consumes it. Record this in a plan doc before Phase 3 or G Stage 2 starts, or PhoneListener's 731 scarred lines get extracted twice. (5) worker.py contention — H Stage 1, E, and B all edit brain/worker.py; the order small-to-large (H, E, B) is deliberate, and B's funnel extraction rebases on their landed diffs; B's shadow logs will contain E's budget-refusal reasons, which must not be misread as verdict diffs. (6) Shared measurement discipline — A (§8), C (pre-registered floors), and H (frozen death criterion) all fix pass criteria before measuring; B should adopt the same for its shadow flip criteria, currently the loosest ('clean diffs' undefined, satisfiable by a quiet week). MERGED-WORK OPPORTUNITIES: B's soak days absorb D (disjoint files) and optionally H Stage 2 (disjoint files); F's Apple-latency days absorb G Stage 0 and step-2 prep. GAPS NO CLUSTER OWNS, both leg-6-critical: (a) external TestFlight Beta App Review — VALID processing is not stranger-installable; assigned to F as a required change; (b) the cold-start path itself — fresh owner provisioning, Twilio number, empty memory DB, day-zero interview, welcome text as a NON-owner experiences them — untested by any recommendation; assigned to step 9 as a mandatory rehearsal before the real stranger. Also screen the recruited stranger's hardware early (iOS version decides whether A Phase 3 can help their week at all).

verdicts.attacks: Attempted kills: (1) Law 1 on EnrollmentInvite's >=3-unnamed-voices threshold — failed: it decides interruption budget on roster STATE, not what words mean; (2) Law 5 on Phase 3's SpeechAnalyzer arm — failed: engine tier is reached only through the spec's pre-registered §8 gate, which I verified verbatim at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-24-voice-capture-design.md:243-245 (shard <25%, speaker populated, capture <60%); (3) never-build — SpeechAnalyzer arm is not on the list and keeps the SFSpeech arm for the iOS 16 floor and contextualStrings (gate leg 7); (4) claim-audit — every cited landing checked in code: capture stamps (AnticipyBackend.swift writes capture_started_at/spoken_at/capture_ended_at from one instant, exactly the 'all three equal the flush instant' the optional refinement fixes; pendingSince exists and is read in flushTail), flushReason/cutContinues (TranscriptFlushPolicy.swift:128-177), parent_line ceiling marking, ListenJournal wiring, worker capture_key with implausible-stamp refusal, segments on-by-default; and every claimed absence confirmed: 8 tejas_gate legs, no EnrollmentInvite.swift, no VAD anywhere in app/ios, no hear_segment/triage_segment in brain/, no gap_before_ms/boot_id writers; (5) single-session sample-size attack on the §8 branch — weakened but not fatal: the criteria were frozen in advance precisely so one honest measurement beats indefinite vibes, and the alternative candidates all spend more on unproven causes. The recommendation is the laws applied: Law 3 is its centerpiece (8 repo-green commits declared unproven until the live session), Law 5's order is exact (senses/context landed, engine last on evidence), VAD correctly killed as zero-consumer instrumentation.

Attempted kills: (1) Law 1 on the direct-address fast lane — failed: the wake-name strip exists at anticipy_core.py:1313-1315 and _RECALL_RE can only ACCELERATE a model judgment (miss cost <=90s of flush latency, never suppression), squarely inside the standing-tape allowance for cheap sifts; the design's refusal of CAPTURE-ARCHITECTURE Trigger A's imperative word-list (verified at CAPTURE-ARCHITECTURE.md:80-81, which even proposes is_consequential as the valve — B correctly swaps in decision.touches) is the right Law-1 call; (2) Law 2 — failed to kill: this is the strongest tape story of the eight — shard_too_thin's TAPE docstring and leg 2's declared flip-to-absence both verified in source (anticipy_core.py:581-612, tejas_gate.py leg_2 'flips to testing its REMOVAL'), and the design deletes the tape atomically with the leg rewrite; (3) Law 5 inversion (context built while capture is 33%) — failed: this IS Law 5 step 2, A's Phases 1-2 recover zero words anyway, and shadow runs on real production inputs; (4) the named killer, double-acting — failed: cursor-advance-before-model (claim() shape verified), [NEW]-only instruction, and _queue_job dedupe are three independent belts, and shadow catches the class against live traffic before any job can mint; (5) rewrite check — candidate B correctly rejected as the forbidden rewrite; the _ambient_verdict extraction preserves every named guard (goal_tokens diff, invented_names, digit guard — all located in source); (6) feed breakage — the 'segmented' claim stamp + post-judge PATCH + crash sweep close the Thinking-forever window; a crash-window event still reaches judgment via the segment cursor. Near-misses worth pinning in tests, not kills: fast-lane behavior when decision.touches is None (falls to the existing fallback funnel — acceptable, and improves once H Stage 1 lands), and the double-stamp of echo events (segmented then ignore).

Confirmed the design's central hole first-hand: the ambient go-ahead gate at anticipy_core.py:1371-1372 is `not dictated and speaker != "other" and channel != "sms" and not in_conversation(context)` — no in_meeting condition, so an armed meeting's bare 'let's do it' can release the freshest held card. Verified every claimed instrument gap: tagForLatestUtterance returns ONLY the tag (score dies inside identify()), ListenJournal has no speaker event and no Views file references ListenJournal/ShareLink (the 'exportable from Settings' comment is a lie today), proof/voice_roster.py:131-138 still returns other:{pid} where VoiceRoster.swift returns 'unknown' (divergence real), speaker_live_test.py pins the zh-cn embedding model. Attempted kills that failed: (a) Law 5 on refusing the Brief's 'unattributed lines never mint' — the refusal is correct (97% no-verdict measured, confirmation gate verified at :1786-1801 as the attribution of last resort; the bar would be deafness, the recorded 2026-08-04 failure); (b) never-build — candidate D (cloud diarization) named-and-refused, journal exports scalars only on an owner tap; (c) the born-red gate leg is a gate, not tape — legal. THE KILL THAT LANDED: the design edits the guard AROUND _GO_AHEAD_RE while its law_notes wave it through as 'pre-existing and untouched' — but docs/FOLLOWUPS.md item 9 already records _GO_AHEAD_RE (anticipy_core.py:1025-1029) as 'a standing LAW 1 violation' whose fix is Law 5 (a model with conversation context decides consent), and it carries NO TAPE: comment and NO red gate leg. Law 2 says tape with no expiry is a rejected diff; touching this exact release path without giving the tape its leg repeats the under-flagging Law 6 exists to catch — cluster E set the precedent by registering _NON_ANSWER.

verdicts.attacks: Every cited mechanism verified in brain/memory.py: profile_facts schema has no status/superseded columns, SAME_FACT_SYSTEM is strictly binary ({"same":bool}), _find_same_fact's 0.4/0.8 sift and number-change path match the cited lines, salience at the profile_facts read is importance x 0.5^(age/30) with confidence absent, confidence is bumped (min(0.99, c+0.15)) and — confirmed by grep — read by zero code outside memory.py; run_nightly_consolidation exists and is called at worker.py:3433; recall consults profile first; _answer_from_memory texts profile facts to the owner; fill_gaps_from_memory promotes recalled values into plan params with _UNTRUSTED_SOURCES excluded; tests/llm_fakes.py carries same_verdicts as claimed. Attempted kills: (1) Law 1 — failed: the relation verdict is a model call, the widened person-name candidate net is a sift IN FRONT of the model, the temporal guard compares timestamps and the provenance fence compares source labels (both structure, mirroring the forget_fact fence); (2) Law 5 'structure while deaf' — failed: the model already distills the contradiction, the gap is genuinely storage for the verdict to land, and the design's own framing ('meaning left entirely to the model') is accurate; (3) resurrection adversarial cases (crash-replay, dedup-miss, untrusted-retires-owner, veto interplay) — all four are pre-closed in the design and the closures hang on real code seams; (4) wrong-'replaces' false positive — the failure mode is silence about a true fact rather than assertion of a dead one, retired rows stay auditable and vetoable, and the five-pattern live eval bounds it; acceptable. Non-fatal frictions surfaced for execution: the live SMS round-trip must force consolidation outside its quiet-hours gate (needs a rig override), and the live-keyed eval leg does not belong inside tejas_gate — see cross-cutting.

ordering: Recommended execution order, driven by three forces: what is bleeding in production NOW, what gates the stranger week, and which clusters collide in the same files. (1) G Stage 0 (0.5d) — nearly free, converts the latent LOCAL-FIRST violation into a deterministic gate before anything else moves; zero conflicts. (2) F starts immediately and runs as background work (1.5-2.5 focused days but dominated by Apple round-trip latency, so start the clock early): it is the literal distribution gate on done_gate leg 6 and touches nothing the brain clusters touch. (3) H Stages 0-1 (1.5d) — the direct-lane 'world'-declaration drop is a live trust-spine bypass in production today, the fix is surgical, and landing the persisted channel FIRST gives cluster B's funnel a stored field to read instead of prose. (4) A Phases 1-2 (2d) MERGED with C's instrument+protocol into ONE field day: build C's journal scoring instrument before the session, then one cable-installed build 76/77 and one owner hour produces BOTH the capture numbers (A's §8 branch input) and the speaker floors (C's enable/disable verdict) — the single biggest merged-work win available; C's in_meeting go-ahead guard and _GO_AHEAD_RE tape registration land alongside H Stage 1 since both touch anticipy_core release paths. (5) E (2.5-3d) — the outbound ledger must precede any real-texting week and must land BEFORE B's flip so the digest's new durable row and the parked-ask stamp carry the uninvited flag from day one; E and B are the two heavy worker.py editors, so serialize them. (6) D (3d) in parallel with E by a second lane — it lives almost entirely in memory.py and conflicts with nobody; it must beat the stranger's day zero because the interview seeds the facts supersession will correct. (7) B last among pre-stranger (7-9 focused days, shadow soak overlapping E/D calendar time): start its pure pieces once H Stage 1 lands, soak the shadow while E and D finish, and flip — deleting shard_too_thin and rewriting leg 2 — only after the deployed lineage is live-verified and the repo is otherwise quiet, because the flip is the one change that rewrites how every ambient line is judged. POST-STRANGER, in order: H Stage 3 (regex death, only after the parity eval is green live), A Phase 3 (SpeechAnalyzer arm, only if the §8 gate opens it), G Stages 1-4 (build the RecognitionEngine seam ONCE, shared with A Phase 3), then VAD/envelope fields and E's moment batcher. Total pre-stranger load is ~13-16 focused days across two parallel lanes — tight but feasible; if something must slip, B's flip (not its shadow) is the only piece that can move into the stranger week's first days without leaving a known hole open, since shadow mode is production-identical.
cross_cutting: CONFLICTS. (1) Gate-leg collision: A (plan Task 5), C, D, and H each want a 'new tejas_gate leg 9' or equivalent. Assign explicitly: A takes tejas leg 9 (flushReason/parent_line mechanism, per the already-written plan), H's fallback-death leg becomes leg 10, C uses its own overnight/voice_gate.py (its design already offers this), and D's live-keyed supersession eval must NOT go into tejas_gate at all — tejas_gate is fully offline-deterministic today and a leg requiring OPENROUTER_API_KEY would turn the scoreboard red on every keyless machine; house it beside done_gate's keyed legs (done_gate leg 3 is the precedent D itself cites) or a memory_gate. SHARED DECISIONS. (6) One field day serves two clusters: A Phase 2's live session and C's five-condition protocol should be one instrumented session on one cable-installed build — C's Meet-at-speaker-volume condition IS A's Tejas condition; this halves the owner-time cost, and owner time is the product's scarcest resource by its own doctrine. verdicts.attacks: The strongest attack lands: THE RETIRED-ROW MERGE TRAP. D makes _find_same_fact scan superseded rows so a re-stated dead fact merges into the retired row 'instead of resurrecting' — but _find_same_fact returns on first match (verified :880-940), so a GENUINE reversal ('...actually, back with Dana') exact-matches the retired Dana row, merges as evidence with status untouched, and never reaches the relation judgment against the active Maya row. The nightly reconcile samples ACTIVE rows only, so it can never heal it. Result: the owner's correction changes nothing she says — the cluster's own problem statement rebuilt one level down, the same 'what?' trust-destroyer moment. Worse, the proof PINS the broken behavior: the adversarial leg 'restated dead fact merges into the retired row and stays retired' is written with no evidence-recency distinction, so the test suite would enforce the failure. Second attack, survived: the design respects every scarred guard I checked — the veto-survives-merge and provenance-launder guards in _merge_fact (:977-1004) are untouched, the provenance fence mirrors forget_fact's fence, the number-rewrite path (the dinner-at-6-vs-8 scar) is preserved, retired rows stay vetoable, and the ALTER-in-try/except migration follows the vetoed_facts precedent documented at :74-93. Third attack, survived: all four stale-fact consumers verifiably route through profile_facts()/recall(), so the single active-only filter genuinely fixes all sinks — unlike candidate C, which would have put fill_gaps_from_memory (money spent on a dead fact) at risk forever. The three-tier proof (offline scripted, live-keyed eval that refuses to pass without a key per done_gate leg-3 doctrine, deployed-fingerprint + live SMS round-trip) is Law-3 sound.
verdicts.required_changes: Close the trap: when a restatement matches a superseded row AND its evidence timestamp is newer than the superseding row's last_seen_ts, run the three-way relation judgment against the active occupant (allowing reverse supersession: Dana-row reactivated or re-inserted active, Maya-row retired) instead of silently accruing evidence on the dead row. Split the corresponding test into two cases — stale re-derivation (stays retired, the crash-replay guard) versus newer restatement (re-judged against the active row) — and add the got-back-together chain to the five-pattern live eval so the fix cannot regress unmeasured.

verdicts.attacks: Verified: TranscriberClient streams undecoded Opus to Deepgram, the token hook and FOLLOWUPS item 8 match the description, LocalTranscriber is dead code whose naive lifecycle reproduces the documented one-line-per-conversation failure (so reviving it, the seductive option, is correctly killed), tests currently PIN the Deepgram wiring, and the firmware receipt says NOT_FLASHED. Attacks: (1) The Stage-0 gate reads a REPO FILE's claim about hardware state — a flash that forgets to update BUILD_RECEIPT.json leaves the leg green while the violation goes live; this is a Law-3 shaped weakness in a leg justified by Law 2 (repo-state, not live-state), though still strictly better than the prose promise it replaces. (2) The RecognitionEngine extraction touches the most scar-laden 731 lines in the app — the same relocation risk E used to kill its own candidate A — but survives because the pure tests (cursor, flush policy, fuzz, queue stress) travel with it, the alternative is the forbidden rewrite, and cluster A's spec §8 requires this seam to exist anyway; the shared-seam flag with cluster A is correctly raised. (3) FOUND A REAL HOLE: feeding pendant PCM into SpeakerTagger.accept while the phone mic also feeds it interleaves two audio geometries in the ONE ring buffer — VoiceRoster's own comment warns 'a bad row poisons every future match', so dual-feed corrupts tagging and can pollute the roster; the design names recognition-task arbitration but never gates the tagger's input. Also the owner's enrollment embedding is phone-mic; scores against 32kbps-Opus-decoded distant audio are unmeasured, and cluster C explicitly defers pendant-path tagging — so pendant speaker tags ship unproven by C's own standard. (4) The pre-delete shadow WER sends owner-consented clips to Deepgram from the Mac harness — survives on the existing proof/pendant_audio_e2e.py precedent, consent named, customer audio excluded. (5) Post-stranger scoping is correct and the never-build refusals (toggle = rule 1 violated on demand; 'amend the law' refused) are the right kills.

Before pendant speaker tags are trusted, run cluster C's journal-scored protocol once over the pendant path (or ship pendant lines with speaker omitted until then — no verdict is the honest state per the honesty wall). Second attack: the partition fix reads the stored consequence for the PENDING row but the want side (_same_pending:3403 'want_consequential = is_consequential(goal)') is unaddressed — a world-declared, read-worded incoming goal would partition as read and dedupe against a research job, which is byte-for-byte the recorded 2026-08-04 dinner-death scar quoted in that function's own docstring ('a job that changes his world can never be deduped against one that only reads').
